title: Outlook desktop: Create PDF from email that keeps the sensitivity label
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, control paths and commands are supported, and the feature-specific gaps remain appropriately qualified. Two minor corrections would distinguish existing server-side PDF attachment encryption from Outlook export and cite Outlook's general desktop licensing requirement.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0]; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Mandatory labelling in a sensitivity label policy blocks Print to PDF for labelled email in Outlook Desktop.
claims.quote: Outlook Desktop blocks printing to PDF if Mandatory Labeling is enabled. This change is in all M365 channels beginning in January 2024.

claims.claim: The documented Outlook Desktop Print to PDF block began in January 2024.
claims.quote: This change is in all M365 channels beginning in January 2024.

claims.claim: Microsoft's August 2024 support page says Outlook Desktop does not support exporting files to PDF.
claims.quote: This error can be misleading since Outlook Desktop does not support exporting files to PDF.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing Print to PDF route does not preserve the sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Because this option removes the sensitivity label, this option won't be available to users if you're using mandatory labeling.

claims.claim: The existing Print to PDF route loses encryption when encryption is applied.
claims.quote: If users select this option, they are warned that the document or email will lose the protection of the label, and encryption (if applied), and must confirm to continue.

claims.claim: Word, Excel and PowerPoint for Windows support exporting Office documents to PDF.
claims.quote:
Office for Windows: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint support the following methods to convert an Office document into a PDF document:
- File > Save As > PDF
- File > Export > PDF

claims.claim: The documented Word, Excel and PowerPoint PDF conversion preserves the label.
claims.quote: When the PDF is created, it inherits the label with any content markings.

claims.claim: The documented Word, Excel and PowerPoint PDF conversion preserves the label's content markings.
claims.quote: When the PDF is created, it inherits the label with any content markings.

claims.claim: Encrypted PDFs created through the documented Office export can be opened with Microsoft Edge on Windows or Mac.
claims.quote: For Windows, if the label applied encryption, that encryption is also inherited. Encrypted PDFs can be opened with Microsoft Edge on Windows or Mac.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited Office-apps page states that Outlook does not currently support PDF attachments inheriting encryption from a labelled message.
claims.quote: Outlook doesn't currently support PDF attachments inheriting encryption from a labeled message.
claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the Office-apps page, but add: 'Separately, the Message encryption FAQ documents server-side encryption of PDF attachments when enabled in Exchange Online; that is attachment protection, not Create PDF export.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ome-faq, which says 'When you send an email, the Office 365 service encrypts PDF file attachments' and includes new Outlook Desktop, web, Mac, iOS and Android.

claims.claim: The mandatory labelling setting is reached in Microsoft Purview through Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Policy settings > Require users to apply a label to their email or documents.
claims.quote: on the Policy settings page: Select Require users to apply a label to their email or documents.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -AdvancedSettings @{DisableMandatoryInOutlook="True"} exempts Outlook messages from mandatory labelling in supporting apps, rather than configuring document mandatory labelling.
claims.quote: DisableMandatoryInOutlook: Outlook apps that support this setting exempt Outlook messages from mandatory labeling. Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{DisableMandatoryInOutlook="True"}.

claims.claim: The PDF sensitivity policy is under Group Policy User Configuration/Administrative Templates/Microsoft Office 2016/Microsoft Save As PDF and Save As XPS add-ins > Use the Sensitivity feature in Office to apply sensitivity labels to PDFs, configured as Disabled.
claims.quote:
User Configuration/Administrative Templates/Microsoft Office 2016/Microsoft Save As PDF and Save As XPS add-ins:
- Use the Sensitivity feature in Office to apply sensitivity labels to PDFs
Configure this setting to be Disabled.

claims.claim: The Office PDF policy registry setting is HKCU\software\policies\microsoft\office\16.0\common\fixedformat, DWORD disablepdfprotection = 1.
claims.quote: Group Policy registry path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\software\policies\microsoft\office\16.0\common\fixedformat DWORD: disablepdfprotection Value: 1

claims.claim: The Outlook printing workaround is HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Preferences, DWORD disablepdfprotectioninoutlook = 1.
claims.quote: Path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Preferences Name: disablepdfprotectioninoutlook (dword32) Value: 1

claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI setting for the Outlook disablepdfprotectioninoutlook workaround is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "disablepdfprotectioninoutlook" Group Policy admin UI. Read the Print to PDF support page and search results; the feature-specific guidance gives a registry value, not an admin UI control.

claims.claim: Mandatory labelling is a tenant-managed label-policy setting applied to the users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: When the policy setting Require users to apply a label to their email and documents is selected, users assigned the policy must select and apply a sensitivity label in their Office apps.

claims.claim: Learn also documents clearing an email-specific checkbox to exempt email from mandatory labelling.
claims.quote: Then select Next > Next and clear the checkbox Require users to apply a label to their emails. Keep the checkbox selected if you want mandatory labeling to apply to emails as well as to documents.
